record.statement: In a two-sided independent concatenation, use unit-length Brownian segments except at increasingly rare negative-time indices where segments stop on first hitting -1. Characterize frequencies giving backward or two-sided Brownian motion.
record.statement_caveat: The exact deterministic or random schedule is part of the classification; do not invent a schedule and count it as another sourced question.
record.title: Sparse first-passage pieces in a forward Brownian concatenation

record.independent_check: Independence is not needed for this Borel-Cantelli upper bound. Infinite means do not contradict the almost-sure sparse-clock estimate.
record.obstruction: A negligible exceptional time fraction is an asymptotic statement; it does not construct an exact backward Brownian law after a finite random shift. The full frequency classification remains open here.
record.result: For a standard Brownian first hitting time tau of -1, reflection gives P(tau>t)=2 Phi(1/sqrt(t))-1 ~ sqrt(2/pi)t^(-1/2), hence E tau=infinity. If exceptional segment indices are 2^k, then sum_k P(tau_k>epsilon 2^k)<infinity. Borel-Cantelli yields tau_k/2^k ->0 almost surely. Splitting the sum into finitely many early terms and a geometrically weighted tail gives sum_(k<=K) tau_k/2^K ->0.
